items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. You walked after 2 of your scored meals, which is too few to see how it affects you yet.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try not to eat dinner too late, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. You didn't have any scored dinners that started at 8 pm or later, so keep up the good habit.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 14.0 hours, and 92.9% of nights reached 13 hours. In the randomized program, adding the overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points (95% CI -0.06 to 0.0) compared with coaching alone. It looked larger in some blood sugar groups, but the program could not tell the groups apart, so this is the overall number. A check in real people (NHANES) showed no clear link yet.

rejected.text: You're doing a great job with overnight fasting, averaging 14.0 hours and reaching 13 hours on 92.9% of nights. In the program, adding overnight fasting to coaching changed some numbers, but it's still being studied to see how it really helps.
